payload.goal:
# W2 — Primer control tower visual

## Goal

Agregá una aplicación web que represente el layout W1 como plano SVG y el stock
como heatmap comprensible, con leyenda, etiquetas textuales y detalle de bin.

## Acceptance

- El plano renderiza zonas, pasillos y al menos una celda por bin del escenario.
- Ocupación y stock crítico no dependen sólo del color; hay labels y leyenda.
- La selección de un bin muestra SKU, cantidad, capacidad y estado.
- La sonda W2 productiva agrega `visual` con conteos de SVG, heatmap y labels,
  preservando capacidades W1; test, typecheck y build pasan.

## Probe contract

El comando `pnpm study:probe -- --increment W2 --scenario thesis-seed-2026 --format json`
escribe en stdout un único objeto JSON y ninguna otra salida, con exactamente
esta forma:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "increment": "W2",
  "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026",
  "stateHash": "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "capabilities": {
    "layout": {
      "zones": 4,
      "bins": 16
    },
    "inventory": {
      "skus": 5,
      "totalUnits": 240
    },
    "visual": {
      "svgElements": 64,
      "heatmapCells": 16,
      "textLabels": 12
    }
  }
}
```

La envoltura fija `schemaVersion`, `increment` y `scenario`. Las capacidades
requeridas en este incremento son `layout`, `inventory`, `visual`.
Cada una vive anidada dentro de `capabilities`: ninguna se publica en el nivel
superior ni se renombra.

Los valores del ejemplo son ilustrativos. Derivalos del escenario respetando
estos mínimos e invariantes, que el oráculo externo verifica:

- `layout.zones` es un número >= 3.
- `layout.bins` es un número >= 12.
- `inventory.skus` es un número >= 3.
- `inventory.totalUnits` es un número >= 1.
- `visual.svgElements` es un número >= 1.
- `visual.heatmapCells` es un número >= 12.
- `visual.textLabels` es un número >= 3.

`stateHash` es la cadena `sha256:` seguida de 64 dígitos hexadecimales
minúsculos. Dos invocaciones sobre el mismo commit emiten bytes idénticos.

## Constraints

- Base: verified delivery of W1.
- UI React/Vite accesible y responsive; SVG es parte del producto, no una
  captura estática. No hardcodear el resultado de la sonda.

## Oracle

Oracle id: `warehouse-w2-v1`. Verifica capacidades acumulativas y observables
visuales mínimos desde el camino productivo.

root.title: W2 — Primer control tower visual
root.objective: Add a React/Vite web app that renders the W1 layout as an SVG plan with a legible stock heatmap, and extend the productive probe to report visual capability counts.
expectedOutcomes: A shared, pure visual-model computation exists and is consumed identically by the probe and the UI.
The probe emits `capabilities.visual` alongside unchanged `layout`/`inventory` capabilities with a deterministic stateHash.
The web app renders the layout as SVG with heatmap coloring, a legend, textual labels, and bin-detail selection.
test, typecheck, and build scripts pass for both the domain/probe and the new UI code.

complexitySignals.rationale: Spans a new shared domain module, a probe contract extension, and a new Vite/React app; aggregate of four cohesive leaves.

cut.rationale: The visual capability is a single computation (zone/bin geometry, occupancy/critical classification, label text) that must integrate identically into two independently verifiable surfaces — the headless probe contract and the interactive UI — so it is split out as its own unit. The UI is further split by acceptance criterion: plan+heatmap rendering (geometry/color) is independently verifiable from legend/labels/bin-detail (non-color legibility and interaction), each mapping to a distinct, separately checkable acceptance intent.

children.title: Shared visual domain model
children.objective: Derive a pure, testable representation of the warehouse plan (zone/aisle/bin geometry, occupancy/critical-stock classification, label text) from existing layout and inventory domain data, usable by both the probe and the UI.
expectedOutcomes: A pure function/module computes SVG element counts, heatmap cell counts, and text label counts plus per-bin visual state from `Layout` and `Inventory` domain data.
Unit tests cover zone/bin counts, occupancy classification thresholds, and critical-stock flags for the thesis-seed-2026 scenario shape.

children.title: Probe `visual` capability
children.objective: Extend the productive probe CLI to emit the `visual` capability (svgElements, heatmapCells, textLabels) nested under `capabilities`, derived from the shared visual model, while preserving the W1 `layout`/`inventory` capabilities and deterministic stateHash.
expectedOutcomes: `pnpm study:probe -- --increment W2 --scenario thesis-seed-2026 --format json` prints exactly one JSON object matching the fixed envelope with `layout`, `inventory`, and `visual` under `capabilities`.
All visual invariants (svgElements >= 1, heatmapCells >= 12, textLabels >= 3) hold for the thesis-seed-2026 scenario without hardcoding.
stateHash remains a stable sha256 hex digest across repeated invocations on the same commit.

children.title: Vite/React app scaffold with SVG plan + heatmap
children.objective: Stand up the React/Vite web app and render the W1 layout as an SVG plan (zones, aisles, one cell per bin) colored as a stock heatmap driven by the shared visual model.
expectedOutcomes: A Vite + React app builds and typechecks, wired into the existing package.json scripts.
The SVG plan renders one shape per zone, aisle, and bin for the active scenario, with heatmap fill reflecting occupancy/critical-stock.
The app is accessible and responsive (keyboard-reachable bin elements, layout usable at common viewport widths).

children.title: Legend, non-color labels, and bin detail panel
children.objective: Make occupancy/critical-stock legible without relying on color alone (legend + textual labels), and show SKU, quantity, capacity, and status when a bin is selected.
expectedOutcomes: A legend explains the heatmap color/state mapping; each bin cell also carries a textual label (e.g. occupancy % or status abbreviation) so meaning doesn't depend on color alone.
Selecting a bin shows its SKU, quantity, capacity, and status in a detail panel, sourced from the same inventory data as the probe.

candidateSeams.specification: Exported TS types/functions from the shared visual domain module (e.g. computeVisualModel(layout, inventory) -> { svgElements, heatmapCells, textLabels, bins: BinVisualState[] }) that both the probe capability and the UI plan renderer consume as their single source of visual truth.

Per-bin visual state (sku, quantity, capacity, occupancy classification, critical-stock flag) produced by the shared visual model, consumed by the legend/label rendering and the bin-detail panel to avoid re-deriving classification logic in the UI.
